page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a local 2835 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities across compute and memory subsystems. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top 25% scores in stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, as well as in Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is highly polarized: cached small-block read-only bandwidth reaches a strong 3648.63 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average tier at 116.44 GB/sec and 83.34 GB/sec respectively. Cryptographic and vector execution are accelerated by hardware support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI instructions.

This hardware profile is highly optimized for database operations, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning tasks. Redis SET operations perform in the top 25% at 63.99 million operations per second, and Passmark database operations are similarly strong. While the server handles prompt processing and text generation efficiently for small 135M parameter models, text generation for large 70B parameter models is poor, highlighting a clear tradeoff for heavy generative AI workloads. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and a massive 2835 GB local NVMe SSD makes this instance a cost-efficient choice for resource-dense general-purpose workloads, enterprise databases, and CI/CD pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it features a 2835 GB local NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable. Benchmark results place its compute performance in the top 25%, with strong scores in multi-core processing, software compilation, and database operations. While cached memory bandwidth is exceptional, uncached large-block memory operations perform at average speeds. Lacking a GPU, it handles small LLM inference tasks efficiently but struggles with large-scale model text generation. This instance is highly suited for enterprise databases, CI/CD pipelines, and general-purpose workloads requiring high local storage capacity and balanced compute resources.
